# Wiktionary

> > A comprehensive multilingual dictionary providing detailed etymologies, pronunciations, grammatical forms, and definitions for words across languages including Latin, English, Russian, and more.

Wiktionary is a collaborative, free-content dictionary that documents words from all languages with extensive linguistic information. Each entry includes International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA) pronunciations, grammatical inflections (declensions, conjugations), etymology, and usage examples, serving as a detailed reference for language learners, linguists, and translators.

## Key Topics

- International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA)
- Latin grammar and declension
- Classical Latin
- Verb conjugation
- Grammatical inflection
- Pronunciation guides (General American, Received Pronunciation)
- Noun and adjective forms
- Dative and ablative cases
- Infinitive and imperative moods
- Etymologies
- Multilingual definitions
- Slang terminology
- Russian language
- Genitive and plural forms

## Latin Grammar and Inflections

- [pluribus - Wiktionary, the free dictionary](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/pluribus): Classical Latin adjective form: dative/ablative plural declension
- [debere - Wiktionary, the free dictionary](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/debere): Latin verb conjugation entry showing infinitive and imperative forms
- [cruris - Wiktionary, the free dictionary](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/cruris): Latin noun form: genitive singular inflection entry

## English Words and Forms

- [started - Wiktionary, the free dictionary](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/started): English verb form: past tense/participle with GA and RP pronunciation
- [street credibility - Wiktionary, the free dictionary](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/street_credibility): English uncountable noun: slang term alternative form definition

## Russian Language Entries

- [заткнись - Wiktionary, the free dictionary](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/заткнись): Russian perfective verb: imperative mood form with IPA pronunciation
